findings.summary: Forex data source is specified as Twelve Data M5, but the search method is described as H1 family/hour/entry-geometry coordinate search. The M5→H1 aggregation step is not specified. Any resampling must use fully-closed M5 bars only (no partial/forming bar included in an H1 close) and must be timestamp-aligned to exchange session boundaries, or the same-bar SL logic will be silently anticipating information not yet available at H1 decision time.

Current date (2026-08-25) is ~3 weeks past the stated 'early-August onward' FINAL boundary. That means FINAL-period bars now exist and are chronologically adjacent to active DEV/VALIDATION work. Temporal proximity increases the risk of incidental FINAL exposure (shared caches, shared data pulls, analysts eyeballing recent charts). Require an explicit, logged data-access boundary (e.g., a hard cutoff date enforced in the data loader, not just an analyst convention) proving FINAL bars were never read, plotted, or summarized during coordinate search.

94 independent per-symbol searches over family × hour × entry-geometry coordinates, filtered to a ≥80% win-rate / positive-expectancy bar, is a large multiple-hypothesis-testing surface. Without a pre-registered search-space size and a multiple-testing correction (or a held-out re-validation pass per symbol before promotion), a nontrivial fraction of 'passing' symbols will be statistical artifacts of the grid size rather than real edge, even with zero data leakage.

V64/V69/V73 are correctly scoped as 'exposed development, hypothesis-seed only,' but the audit should confirm the coordinate-search grid itself (which families/hours/geometries are even considered) was not narrowed based on what performed best in that exposed window. A narrowed search space is a subtler form of the same leakage the FINAL-tuning ban is meant to prevent, even if FINAL bars are never touched directly.

'94 symbols, independent, no pooling' describes the trade-construction process, but does not establish statistical independence of outcomes. Correlated instruments (e.g., BTC/ETH, or correlated forex majors) sharing regime-driven moves can make apparently-independent per-symbol validation passes co-move, inflating confidence in the aggregate 80%+ win-rate claim. This should be reported as a caveat alongside any cross-symbol summary stat, not silently assumed away by 'no pooling.'

OKX-first with 'continuity-checked' fallbacks for crypto H1 needs the continuity check itself specified (max allowed gap/price discontinuity at a provider-switch point) — otherwise a fallback stitch can create an artificial gap that the same-bar SL logic misreads as a favorable or adverse fill that would not occur on a single unbroken feed.

The contract forbids silent eligible-day deletion but the plan as described doesn't specify a reporting mechanism. Any day excluded from the 1–3 eligible-execution window (missing bar, provider gap, holiday) must be logged with a count and reason per symbol, not merely dropped from the eligible-day denominator.

review.proposal: Approve the bounded per-symbol DEV/VALIDATION geometry search in principle, conditional on: (1) making the M5→H1 aggregation rule explicit and leakage-safe; (2) enforcing a hard, code-level FINAL-period data cutoff with an access log, given FINAL bars now exist as of 2026-08-25; (3) pre-registering the coordinate search-space size per symbol and applying a multiple-testing correction (or a second held-out validation slice) before any symbol is promoted past the 80% win-rate / positive-expectancy bar; (4) confirming the search grid itself was not shaped by V64/V69/V73 outcomes, only used as a bounded hypothesis seed; (5) logging (not silently dropping) any excluded eligible day and any crypto fallback-provider stitch point with its continuity delta; (6) reporting cross-symbol correlation as a caveat on any pooled summary statistic even though no pooling occurs in trade construction. No performance claim should be made until a single deterministic replay against untouched FINAL data reproduces the DEV/VALIDATION result bar-for-bar.

findings: The plan does not define immutable DEV/VALIDATION date ranges or a formal embargo separating data known through 2026-07-31 from the untouched early-August FINAL period.
“Exact instrument data” is not yet auditable: venue, instrument ID, contract type, timezone, candle-boundary rules, price adjustment, provider version, and raw-file hashes are unspecified.

Continuity-checked crypto fallbacks can alter market microstructure and violate exact-instrument requirements unless substitutions are predeclared, provenance-preserving, and never splice economically different instruments.
Eligible-day logic is underspecified. A deterministic calendar and reason-coded accounting for every excluded symbol-day are required to prevent silent deletion.

The bounded coordinate search lacks explicit candidate grids, search order, tie-breaking, stopping rules, and validation-selection rules, so researcher degrees of freedom and multiple-testing bias remain uncontrolled.
Conservative same-bar SL handling is directionally sound but must specify collisions among entry, stop, target, gaps, and multiple signals without intrabar assumptions.
The 1–3 executions constraint needs deterministic signal ranking, concurrency, duplicate-entry, session-boundary, and forced-exit rules.
The 80% minimum win-rate and positive-expectancy requirements need minimum trade counts and uncertainty reporting; point estimates alone are insufficient.
Earlier V64/V69/V73 evidence is correctly labeled hypothesis-only, but all seeded families, hours, and geometries must be registered before VALIDATION to prevent legacy-informed adaptive tuning.
No performance claim is supportable from the supplied context; deterministic replay artifacts and results were not provided.
review.proposal: Before research, freeze a machine-readable protocol containing: the 94-symbol universe with no deletion; canonical instrument/provider mappings; raw-data hashes and provenance; UTC candle construction and continuity rules; immutable DEV, VALIDATION, and FINAL boundaries with an embargo; complete bounded parameter grids; deterministic search order, tie-breakers, and stopping criteria; conservative event-order rules; explicit eligible-day and 1–3 execution logic; and reason-coded exclusion logs. Permit fallback data only when it represents the same instrument and candle semantics; otherwise mark the interval unavailable without silently removing eligible days. Conduct all refinement on DEV, select once using predeclared VALIDATION criteria with multiplicity controls and minimum sample-size/confidence requirements, then lock code, configuration, dependencies, and data hashes. Replay FINAL exactly once with no tuning. Report every symbol independently, including failures and unavailable intervals, plus aggregate summaries that do not substitute for per-symbol compliance.

review.proposal: Proceed with the bounded per-symbol geometry research as specified. For DEV/VALIDATION-only refinement, I propose: (1) For each symbol, enumerate the coordinate grid (family, hour, entry geometry) but cap the number of configurations per symbol to avoid overfitting, e.g., max 50 configurations per symbol, and require a minimum of 30 eligible days per configuration to be considered. (2) Use a deterministic replay script that logs all parameters, data versions, and execution timestamps to ensure reproducibility. (3) Validate the same-bar SL rule on a small holdout subset (e.g., 10% of eligible days) before full validation, but never use the final period for tuning. (4) For crypto fallbacks, document any continuity-check failures and ensure the fallback data source is consistent with OKX timestamps to avoid lookahead. (5) For forex M5, aggregate to H1 only using the exact provider's timestamps, and verify no weekend gaps are misinterpreted. (6) After validation, if any symbol fails the 80% win rate or positive expectancy, do not delete it; instead, mark it as non-tradeable and report it transparently. (7) All results must be stored with a hash of the input data and code version to enable deterministic replay. These refinements stay within the bounded plan and do not touch the final period.
